Armored fingers made of toughest iron; it's no coincidence they resemble the crooked hand of a skeleton.
An elite pair of leg guards, forged black as night and outfitted with lethal toe talons.
"And the reach of God's many hands will be like a great golden flame, billowing up into the darkness."  - Madrigal Erinth
"Good business is knowing the business of others." -overheard in Havenport
When the Lords of Eversol shake hands, it is said that the truth passes between their palms, even as their lips speak lies.
Leg guards belonging to a Lord of House Orland. Woe betide the thief who is caught wearing them.
Adorned with blackened skulls, it seems that the judgment of its mysterious owner is always death.
Caked with soot and salt, did its former owner step from the sea or climb out of the bowels of the earth?
These glowing eyes are a false moon, a deadly beckoning. What the candle says to the moth.
These greaves match the bootprints left in the caved-in chests of Risen and Sacrament Guards alike.
A luxurious pair of trousers "retrieved" from some distant corner of the Far Lands.
Yes, the bird comes with it.
An oddly-hewn set of gauntlets that seem to offer little physical protection - but their strength may not be visible to the naked eye.
A garment that some claim was stitched together out of threads from beyond the known realms of existence.
The black cloth of this death cult seems to swallow all light, even in the midst of the day.
How many bodies have gone cold beneath the pitiless squeeze of these gloves?
The Reapers wear a mask of death - their god, their purpose, their gift to the world.
The Reapers move quiet as the grave, which is the one true home they seek to deliver us all to.
Inquisitors, Seraphs, and Keepers all share one thing in common - they serve the Madrigal.
Let the hands of God enfold your mind. And you will realize that you have always been Embraced.
There are some churches sprinkled around the realm whose doors mysteriously never open. No one but the Inquisition knows their true purpose.
All paths lead to the Embrace.
It is said that the holy Keepers never speak, for there is no word as swift as God's wrath.
No one has ever seen a Keeper without its helm. In fact some say they are empty; and God himself gazes out through the many eyes.
A Madrigal's Keeper leaves no footsteps, for God's hands carry them wherever they go.
The luminous gloves of one who gave his life to protect his Madrigal - the sacred dream of every Keeper.
The official armor of the elite leaders of the Knights of House Bolein. Few and fervent are those who earn the right to wear it.
The Knights of House Bolein are the pillars upon which Phalen stands tall.
The glove of a soldier knows only how to clutch a weapon. But the glove of a leader knows how to shake the enemy's hand.
It is said the plumage on the helm of a Primus comes from the rare pheasants that are bred in the king's private garden.
We are born in a roar. We must die in the quiet.
Words cannot be grasped, but weapons can.
Speak only purpose, and reap only quiet. The Sayer hears our deeds.
No name shall be called, no words shall be spoken. But my footfalls you will hear.
A weapon of graceless efficiency. Archers and knights look down on it, until you're looking down on them.
It's said a betrayed archer spent years hunting down her former allies and impaling their skulls on her bow.
Lined with a hush of rare feathers, this bow seems to vanish when leaned against a tree.
Arrows loosed from it always seem to grow something where they land.
The Archers of Halheim say a bow must be held as if it were the nape of an animal's neck. Tender, and gentle - but ready to send a message at any moment.
A bow of eerie white that never seems to dirty - mud and blood alike slide off it like water.
The woodland bow of a hunter so patient, moss eventually overgrew him, leaving only the bow behind.
A short ranged bow for novice archers or those wishing to remain discrete.
When strung, it hums just above hearing. Some archers report strange dreams and uncanny aim.
A bow of unconventional design that musters up considerable strength from its short draw.
A short bow polished to a mirror sheen - for archers swift enough that they don't care about being spotted.
Made from the antlers of a whole herd of deer, it brings luck only to those who hunt for food, not sport.
Strong yet lissome, some say a yew bow won’t fire unless the shot feeds a stomach or ends a monster.
The ghastly hook of the Deadtide's leader, who was driven mad by the fumes of a plagued whale carcass.
A heavy lantern enwreathed in strange growths. They seem to feed off the light within.
A light in darkness, a pool of warmth in the cold. Many mistake its glow for safety.
A lantern carved out of a human skull that still manages to light the way... only the way towards what?
Held in left hand, brightens dark areas. Time-limited usage, <color=#F2E6BD>loses durability over time</color> while equipped.
The skull of a traveler who froze to death amid icy peaks - you can still hear the wind howl through its sockets.
Allows the wielder to fire <color=#F2E6BD>explosive arrows</color> with a <color=#F2E6BD>Bow</color>.
Allows the wielder to fire <color=#F2E6BD>blighted arrows</color> when equipped with a <color=#F2E6BD>Bow</color>.
Allows the wielder to fire <color=#F2E6BD>frost arrows</color> when equipped with a <color=#F2E6BD>Bow</color>.
Allows the wielder to fire <color=#F2E6BD>lightning arrows</color> when equipped with a <color=#F2E6BD>Bow</color>.
Sometimes a battle is like a verbal joust, with barbs traded back and forth. This ends the conversation.
A formidable shield, dyed red for one very specific reason.
The leader of the Risen has seen the glint of just about every blade on Sacra. But none have ever passed this wall.
The sigil of House Bolein reminds us there is no rebirth without death, and for one body to be warmed, another must be burned.
A greatshield forged in the mines of Tir. As timeless and immovable as the mountain herself.
May glory be found upon the open seas, and may God's embrace be found in death.
The last defense of the Inquisition, emblazoned with the reach of the one true God.
In your attacks, be as swift as the wind. In your defense, be as solid as a tree.
For the Risen, the leviathan symbolizes the people – long dormant, but mighty when woken by the abuses of those in power.
The Gloam burrows through flesh and bone and caverns of stone - why would steel be any different?
A powerful shield hammered by a reclusive cult of druids from Waithe, about which little is known.
The undulating formations of Seethe regiments have been known to confuse if not outright dizzy opposing troops.
A grotesque barrier of unknown origin. May God forgive the wretch who wields it.
A shield like any other, only more so.
Every divot on this shield is a mark of glory. Until the one that pierces it through.
A shield polished and buffed until your enemies can see themselves in it. Do them the kindness of offering a closer look.
A pockmarked circle of steel offering a thin veil of protection.
Defend yourself with the ferocity of a lion; or else flee with the haste of a stag.
Only the most desperate of times should pit weathered wood against steel weapons.
In a land of giants and monsters, some armorers consider it poor form to paint a beast of imagination, lest it might spring to life.
For her soldiers, House Bolein and the Empire are one and the same. Arrogant perhaps, but not inaccurate.
"A good shield is like a doorway to the heart. It must never be opened."  -Lorig the Blacksmith
The symbol of Sacrament. The color of an uncertain dawn. The hope to survive just one more day.
"Catch a fish, catch a cold, catch a secret 'fore you're told" - Havenport children's song
A rare and unusual shield not forged in Phalen, despite its prominent eye. Rumors say it was hammered by a mad tinker somewhere in the Shattered Hand.
An elegant shield bearing the sigil of a long-forgotten family, most likely from Thorn.
Bright like the boldness of the morning sky. Unyielding like the spirit of the great House Wallace.
The shield of an adolescent squire, one who has yet to take a life on the battlefield.
A powerful shield rumored to be the demented creation of a Balak Taw warlord - but no one knows for sure.
A sleek and swift defender, one of the finest of its kind - but beaten ragged from years of battle.
An elegant kite shield forged in Phalen and brought to Sacra as an heirloom of the Bolein family.
A popular rumor among sailors is there's only one substance that can protect a shield against saltwater rust.
Marauders from Thorn are said to summon the four corners of the compass in battle - courage from the west; cunning from the east; fury from the south; and despair from the north.
Compact and colorful, built to feel like part of your arm.
Whether the bearer of this shield prevails, or falls in battle; it is meant to be.
"Sickness makes a noise. And it's not a moan or a hiss - it's a ghastly CRACK." - unknown deathbed ravings
"Our final death is a debt owed. Each small death is a payment toward it." - Elegy of the Silent
"The eternal gods know only the world as it was, the Born God sees the world as it could be." - Litany of Hope
"Let their screams be our battle cry. Let their whimpers be our last words." - Elegy of the Unspoken
"All things fester. Flesh to fluid. Bone to dust. You to this. To us." - Prayer of Rot
"Part the branches and steady the wind, oh Seeker, so that I may take flight." - Hymn of Freedom
"The Born God sees through our eyes, acts through our hands. He is countless, he is legion." - Litany of Union
"Our god is the Born God. Not the first god, but the last. Not the question, but the answer." - Litany of Origin
"The Born God subsumed the kingdom of gods, now our duty is to subsume the kingdom of men." - Litany of Duty
"Feel unwell. Feel nothing. Feel this blessing of decay." - Prayer of Sickness
"We are mother to the plague and child to it. We eat our young. We eat our old." - Elegy of the Empty
"The Born God knew you in the beforelife, as he will again in the afterlife. Are you worth knowing?" -  Litany of Fealty
"The Sayer speaks for us. So we cloak ourselves in silence." - Elegy of the None
"They want what you have. They are what you want. Take." -  Prayer of Betrayal
"We grow, we build, we search, we pass. But only with all four do we live." - Hymn of Four
"A name is a weakness. A voice is a vice. We have neither." - Elegy of the Hushed
"Eat the moving. Feast upon the still. All is hunger." - Prayer of Appetite
"Look away, oh Forsaken, I am not ready." - Hymn of Loss
"All practice our faith, even if they do not know its name. There are no infidels, only heretics." - Litany of Embrace
"You have been wronged. You have been curdled. They must hurt for it." - Prayer of Agony
"Place your lips to the earth, oh Mother, and breathe warmth into my harvest." - Hymn of Growth
"Thread your fingers through my own, oh Maker, and shape the clay of my becoming." - Hymn of Form
Favored by the Boarskin clan, this rugged axe features a jagged edge mimicking the ferocity of a wild boar's tusks.
A simple axe carried by hunters to make a fast shelter or a faster kill.
"May the grass grow over your bones" - a blessing and a curse uttered by the tribesmen bearing this axe.
A battle axe, well-worn but still sharp. It has cleaved many men and seen what lies within.
The jagged edges of this axe are a particular cruelty, and a reminder of the cost of crossing Phalen.
In your hands it feels light as a feather, sunk into your foe’s skull it feels heavy as the hereafter.
Some claim the Harvesters growl “timber” when they cleave a man in two, a vestige of their old selves buried beneath their madness.
Designed by Royal Executioner Rochel himself, ideal for deaths delivered without hesitation nor mercy.
Its few surviving victims argue over what’s worse – the going in or the pulling back out.
Pray that the screams of its victims drown out the wet grinding crunch of its progress.
A weapon for those in desperate times. Swing first, swing hard, and hope for the best.
It is like the life of man: nasty, brutish, and short.
Not all fires bring warmth – some offer instead an everlasting cold.
The ancient method of its forging saw it buried in sand for forty nights. Modern blacksmiths eschew this step.
The "eye" affixed to its cross guard is more than decorative - it's a counterbalance for precise strikes.
This sword's forked point serves no purpose other than brutality. But, at times, brutality is a purpose.
Legend says if you carve the name of your enemy into its hilt, it will only shatter upon their demise.
A fisherman's blade, it severs cleanly and without fuss.
A well-weighted scimitar of simple design commonly seen dangling from Risen belts.
The Grifkin goat men model these blades after ram horns - ideal for swift disembowelings.
Upon joining the Sailor's Guild, one is issued a compass, an Ashen Sea map, and a scimitar. All will be used.
The weapon of choice for knights of the now-disgraced House of Mar'quat.
A well-crafted dagger is the great leveler - it slides equally into the bellies of drunks and backs of kings.
One grieves for even the animals laid to rest with such a twisted blade.
A simple, versatile knife preferred by hunters. If there is a job to be done, it will do it.
"A knife is like a poor secret, whispered deep and often." - old proverb
The assassins of Myrfall are said to carry such blades, to make short work of those judged unworthy of living.
It's tradition to use the remnants of an exhausted forge to make one final, monstrous hammer.
It splits stone and skulls alike - a mountain of purpose focused on a single point.
They can be seen dotting the Frozen Peaks, memorials to those who gave their life to the climb.
It is unknown if the stone was chiseled into the face of a man, or if a man's skull was transformed into stone.
An unsually supple hammer said to originate from the blind Stone Tappers of The Seethe.
Once a year, a troupe of Havenport bards use this hammer for music. The other 364 days its use is violence.
A tool of "re-education" often used by the more enthusiastic of Caylen's devotees.
Some weapons blur the line between instrument of war and instrument of torture.
The Balak Taw learn all the worst lessons from their winged brothers - such as how to impale an enemy.
Only once the silence is complete - one crushing blow at a time - will the Cerim's task be fulfilled.
Shaped in a "cold stone forge," they're said to strike faster beneath the glow of the moon.
A blacksmith's wife caught her husband cheating and used one to skewer him toe to crown. The name stuck.
The Morgana "Mud Men" Uprising saw much use of these wicked spikes of iron, pin-cushioning Atlan knights.
A rapier of such surgical precision that some claim they can feel a slight tug of it pulling toward a foe's heart.
A blade forged from the severed horn of a Siren Queen, a creature rarely seen and almost never survived.
A falcon relies not on subterfuge not guile, but speed alone. This blade is no different.
The men of Arvos use these spears both to keep enemies at bay and test the sinking sands' depth.
A spear of Kylesh design, where emeralds litter the island shoals like iridescent boulders.
A rustic harpoon designed to bury itself in a whale's hide and not let go.
A common spear, simple but effective, often carried by the Sworn Guards of Sacrament.
Its fluted tip is as pleasing to the eye as it is damaging to any tissue it penetrates.
A wedged jousting lance meant for splintering shields and the bones they protect.
Eight of these spears plunged into the 26th Governor of Sacrament at once, executing her for her crimes.
Imperfections in steel traditionally lead to weakness, but this sword's blend of twin metals imparts strength.
Rusted by blood and weary from death, this sword carries out its duty with grim purpose.
A cursed weapon reputed to hold its victims' souls eternally in the moment of their demise.
The governor's short sword serves as a promise - to keep his aspirations and his enemies in striking distance.
The governor's long sword serves as a reminder - to seek peace by any means necessary, including war.
It reeks of the swamp's wretched bargain - a fast death by blade or a slow one by sickness.
A great slab of a sword etched with the stories of an unknown, long dead people.
All of the forest's fury sealed within a blade of pure light. Glowing wisps drift from its surface like willow branches.
Some swords seek out the tiniest of openings, while others carve their own.
A training sword for a squire - used in combat only by the overconfident, the deranged, or those in dire straits.
A decayed and pitted sword, blackened by the dark deeds of former masters.
A sword that strikes swift as a viper, the air hissing as it's riven.
A sword from the isle of Thorn - you can still smell the saltwater in its hilt.
This wickedly long blade is meant to end a fight before a foe has a chance to start one.
Everything has a price. Even knowledge. Especially knowledge.
As the rank mass dribbles away, so too does the wand’s potency, leaving only the stain of sweetness.
Some doors, once opened, can be hard to shut.
The more gnarled the tree, the more magic one might find entangled in its roots.
A strange assemblage of mystical totems, unified only by the dark will of its wielder.
All wands are hungry. It’s up to its wielder to determine for what.
The Born God has many hands – see what damage just one can do.
On the Isle of Kull, wheat is ice-shorn with these mystic wands – threshed and frozen for winter in a single swing.
All wands are unholy, but those made from human remains dally with the most wretched of forces.
The embers should burn its branches. The branches should crush the embers. Magic abhors reason.
It's not your reflection you see in its cracked visage, it's a small sliver of yourself lost forever.
“One hitch to tie your garter, one weave to warm your bed. One stitch to hold the dark at bay, one knot to crack your head.” - nursery rhyme
Put your ear to this wand, and you’ll hear dark whispers. Put your eye to it, and you’ll never see again.
What magic simmered in the head of a plagued boar? And what sick soul saw fit to craft with it?
In the Phalen religion, magic is blasphemy, so the church’s more mystical adherents simply practice “acts of faith.”
A weapon once radiant with holy purpose now worn down to a fine sinew of steel.
The raiders of Darshem only attack at noon, holding these swords aloft to blind enemies with their shine.
Ashes from the forge are rubbed into their surface, dulling their shine but sharpening their point.
Daggers designed for rapid, deep punctures to desanguinate with ease.
"Which blade will stand watch while the other sleeps? Neither, my blades never rest." - old Kylesh proverb
It's a cruel irony that the more a dagger decays, the more viciously it tears into flesh.
A rogue's dagger should be forged as a rogue's life is lived - not too short, not too long, and ending swiftly.
When a body is discovered at daybreak with three deep rents down its back, authorities know to leave well enough alone.
A diamond is harder than bone, and it’s happy to prove it.
Long ago a forgotten warrior made a dark bargain, trading flesh for power. This is all that remains.
Late at night, when the world is quiet and still, you can faintly hear it pleading for its next meal.
Not all craftsmen work the loom or potter’s wheel. The Balak Taw know - violence too is an art.
With steel spun fine as a spider’s thread, these blades rip wounds as gaping as a bear's bite.
The Boarskin deliberately leave their blades uncleaned. Infection leads to rot, and rot leads to victory .
The Knights of Tanth popularized this design for both open combat and backroom “questioning”. Answers tend to dislodge as fast as teeth.
Wood rots, cloth frays, stone crumbles, but fury smolders eternal.
It cuts as clean as a surgeon’s scalpel, only its patients rarely recover.
One step above tying rocks to your fists - these gloves are meant to pulp and pulverize. Grace is for dancers.
Some say the sun is fueled by fire. Others insist it’s rage.
War is messy. Why shouldn’t one’s injuries be the same?
Cerim texts contain no reference to a life after the Pestilence is gone.
Simple cloth wraps for those who trust that their fists are plenty hard enough.
A heavy iron axe carried often by bandits, and a testament to the fact that not all threats are hollow.
There is no piece of nature's bounty and grace that the Boarskin can't defile.
A shattered axe, having long since left pieces of itself buried in skulls and rib cages, but still deadly.
Those who can no longer hear the Sayer over the howl of their own madness should be pitied. Pitied and feared.
"Paint your axe gold, so that your enemies may mistake the shine in their skull for heaven." - old proverb
Before being twisted into Harvesters, many woodsmen would set camp for their families near the forest. Hence the oldest blood on their axes.
In the legend of Huro, he used his axe to fell an entire forest, as well as the minor god he angered in doing so.
Not all great axes are graceless, brutal weapons. But this one is.
It's considered a sign of respect from the Riders of Langold if they face you with the longer of twin axe faces.
The Dasha people of Marin eschew weapons, but their sturdy axes don't care how they're put to use.
It's an ongoing debate as to whether giants ever roamed the land. Clubs such as these keep the question open.
No dawn follows the blow of an Evening Star.
As one counts the years ringed on a tree trunk, one can count the lives smeared on this massive staff.
A strange growth cut from a holy tree - it continues to grow with each swing, as if fed by blood.
Studded with small, strange faces, it's said to be the burial tool for a long lost hill tribe.
A sickly stone affixed to a shaft. Perhaps it will shatter tomorrow. Perhaps never.
The blood, bones, and flesh of fallen warriors woven into a grotesque amalgamation.
Originally designed for shattering unruly stones, it seems to take greater pleasure doing the same to skulls.
The tooth of an unknown monstrosity. With any luck, its owner is no longer searching for it.
A tree trunk forms a crude but effective mallet, used by those Risen raiders weighty enough to lift it.
It's said that if a shard of this jagged sword chips off, it will grow in its victim's body, turning their blood to iron.
A remnant of simpler times, when one knight faced another in an open field.
Previously wielded by a plagued monstrosity, no amount of scrubbing seems able to remove the stench.
This towering blade seems heavy with memory - battles won and lost and never fought.
A long buried blade, chewed away by the elements, dragged out of its grave for one final campaign.
A weapon made famous from its use by freedom fighters during the Monksbane Wars.
If its first swing doesn't sever a limb, a few back and forth motions will do the trick.
Used in winter to shear off great blocks of ice, it finds other uses year round.
The brutal, massive blade of an executioner who has lost their purpose but not their calling.
A design that saw great popularity in Phalen until its designer was caught in bed with the King's nephew.
Stamped with the seal of the great smith Tomlin the Third, its blade will cut a falling feather in two.
The knights of Elgarth test their blade's edge by counting the stalks of wheat they can fell in a single swing.
Few sights are more intimidating than a sea of Bolein knights, each hoisting their phoenix beak aloft.
It's tradition for an apprenticing mainland knight to choose the stone to serve as his halberd's counterweight.
A grisly polearm carried often by Havenport guards - Governor Grafston's idea of "justice with teeth."
The scythe of The Reapers - a sadistic death cult - this unholy weapon whispers a dark thirst.
Before the pestilence rotted their minds and limbs, the Nith used such scythes to harvest swampgrass roots.
"Easy to separate a head from a neck, far harder to separate a soul from a body." - Thorn executioner axiom
A Dasha Caretaker's staff, only grown putrid and diseased. Lulling voices can almost be heard wafting from it.
Some say witches still lurk in Sacra's dark corners, crafting tools out of wood, mold, and unlucky creatures.
A dried out hive of spores, tainting the air with each swing, fungi happy to take root inside a foe's lungs.
The cold shatters all things – the spirits of men and their bones as well.
A stave made from a ring of rock that tumbled down from the heavens, its curve strangely perfect.
A staff for those who feed on deception, who mimic their meals rather than confront them.
The pitiful husk of a tree, once burned by lightning; now it harbors the power to burn grown men to ash.
A staff made from a wagon wheel and a fetid urn. There are no limits to man's ingenuity.
For some, atonement is eternal. Shackles cast off, cell opened, but punishment carried with them always.
The long-dead guardians of the Frozen Peaks carried these staffs - like all of winter held in a clenched fist.
A smoldering effigy of occult origins. Whomever holds it speaks for all the forests felled and silenced.
You were born with two fists - might as well put them to use.
